title: Bacteria producing the bioplastic polyhydroxybutyrate kill the nematode Caenorhabditis elegans
experiments_summary: 1. Metabolite-bacteria interaction screen: Eight central carbon metabolites were tested in combination with nine bacterial species on C. elegans growth and survival on metabolite-supplemented NGM plates, with developmental timing assessed relative to controls. 2. Paraformaldehyde (PFA) inactivation: Comamonas was metabolically inactivated with PFA and fed to C. elegans with lactate to determine whether active bacterial metabolism was required for toxicity. 3. Comamonas transposon insertion mutant screen: ~5,500 Comamonas transposon mutants were screened in 96-well format with L1 animals on NGM supplemented with 75 mM lactate; hits were confirmed across three biological replicates, and insertion loci identified by PCR and Sanger sequencing. 4. Metabolite cross-resistance testing: Identified Comamonas mutants were tested for resistance to lactate, pyruvate, and 3-HB to map genetic requirements for PHB biosynthesis pathway steps. 5. Animal recovery/transfer assay: Animals exposed to PHB-producing Comamonas for 24 or 72 hours were transferred to non-PHB-producing Comamonas to assess whether developmental arrest was reversible. 6. C. necator feeding assays: L1 animals were fed Cupriavidus necator H16 (wild-type and PHB-null phaCAB mutant) with and without lactate supplementation to assess developmental outcome. 7. Transmission electron microscopy (TEM): Bacteria (Comamonas wild-type, lldP mutant, E. coli, C. necator) and C. elegans intestinal cross-sections were prepared by chemical fixation and laser-induced fixation, respectively, and imaged to visualize PHB granules and intestinal morphology. 8. GC-MS quantification of PHB: Bacteria grown under various conditions were lyophilized, PHB was extracted and esterified, and methyl-3-hydroxybutyrate was quantified by GC-MS normalized to cell dry weight and an internal standard. 9. Engineered E. coli PHB-production: The phaCAB operon and phaP from Comamonas were cloned into E. coli HT115 (pGG55 construct); PHB production was confirmed by GC-MS and toxicity toward C. elegans was assessed with and without lactate supplementation. 10. Carbon source toxicity panel: C. elegans survival past L1 was quantified on sub-lethal doses of multiple carbon sources (pyruvate, lactate, acetate, glucose, gluconate, 3-hydroxypropionate, butyrate, 3-HB) with four bacterial strains (Comamonas, C. necator, E. coli HT115, engineered E. coli HT115+phaCAB+phaP). 11. Natural microbiota genome analysis: Published genomes of C. elegans-associated microbiota were searched for the phaC gene. 12. C. elegans EMS forward genetic screen: ~10,000 haploid genomes were screened after EMS mutagenesis for survival on Comamonas + 75 mM lactate; one viable mutant was backcrossed, and the causative mutation identified by whole-genome sequencing using sibling subtraction, then confirmed by Sanger sequencing. 13. CRISPR-Cas9 nuc-1 allele generation: Two independent nuc-1 nonsense alleles were generated by frameshift-causing indels and backcrossed three times to N2; survival on PHB-producing Comamonas was quantified. 14. Lawn avoidance assay: 50 L4 animals were transferred to unseeded plates and then to Comamonas (wild-type or phaC mutant) plates; animals inside and outside the lawn were counted ~24 hours later. 15. Pharyngeal pumping rate measurement: ~20 first-day adults were videoed at 20 FPS for 30 s and pumping counted manually at 10 FPS. 16. TEM of nuc-1 mutant vs. wild-type intestines: Animals exposed to Comamonas + lactate for ~12 hours were fixed and imaged as pharynx and anterior intestine cross-sections to compare PHB granule accumulation and pharyngeal grinder morphology. 17. Fluorescent Comamonas feeding and clearance assays: Comamonas strains expressing PhaP::RFP or constitutive RFP were used to feed wild-type and nuc-1 mutant animals; animals were transferred to no-food or non-fluorescent Comamonas and scored for pharyngeal versus intestinal RFP retention. 18. In vivo gut DNA staining: Mixed-stage animals were incubated with ethidium bromide and Comamonas for 30 min, washed, and imaged to confirm undigested bacterial gDNA in nuc-1 mutant intestines. 19. In vitro PHB-gDNA mixing experiments: Purified PHB was mixed with extracted bacterial gDNA and assessed for changes in aqueous solubility and agarose gel electrophoresis mobility. 20. Intestinal calcium imaging: Wild-type and nuc-1 mutant animals expressing intestinal GCaMP6 (Pges-1::NLSwCherry::SL2::GCaMP6) were fed Comamonas ± 75 mM lactate or Comamonas phaC mutant; Ca2+ dynamics were recorded at 15 FPS for 5 min using dual-camera brightfield/fluorescence microscopy, and inter-cycle intervals and kymographs were extracted with custom MATLAB scripts. 21. Smurf intestinal barrier assay: L4 animals pre-exposed for 24 hours to Comamonas ± lactate or phaC mutant (or Cry5B-expressing E. coli as positive control) were fed 1% FD&C Blue #1 dye for 3 hours, recovered on E. coli OP50 for 30 min, and scored for blue dye in intestinal cells versus lumen.
